newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 21.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Banks must bridge the difference between interest lending and deposit rates to help the Greek economy, small and medium-size enterprises and home-buyers, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou urged yesterday, speaking to the general assembly of the Union of Balkan Chambers. Papandoniou predicted an increase in construction activity and said the government would establish a finance investment fund to support major investment in the Balkans, with capital from the US and Europe.

--The general price index span away yesterday from reaching the all-time record it had been inching towards during the past 18 sessions, closing 2.9 percent down at 1,612.71 points, although turnover remained at high levels at 41.5 billion drachmas.
--The deadline for refinancing debts to ETVA bank was extended yesterday to June 30, and there will be no further extension, the bank said.
--An expert committee has recommended wage increases of between 2.5-4.0 percent next year to help the country move towards economic and monetary union.
--The finance ministry is planning to place a supervisor in each taxation department and office to oversee planning, coordination and monitoring of tax audits on taxpayers and businesses.

--The pressure to step up the rate of public revenues is leading the finance ministry to effectively create "two-speed" tax services, differentiating between those bringing better rates of returns. The best performers (30 of the 138 offices brought in 73.3 percent of the seven trillion drachmas of totoal inflows last year) will recieve material and technical support.

--SEV, the Association of Greek Industries, said yesterday the agreement between the two major parties on the need for convergence provides a perfect opportunity to go ahead with privatisation and deregulation of markets.

--The creation of infrastructure projects as a basic lever to increase GDP, as the International Monetary Fund report - to be released today - stresses, and the speeding up of existing projects as well as better absorption of Community funds are the government's priorities at the present time.
--Elections for new administrations of chambers of commerce will be held on December 1-2, it was announced yesterday. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
